_comment: Hand-authored. Loading a special screen and an ordinary room, bank 7 $EE1D-$EF15 (the tables after it are claimed elsewhere). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: LOAD A SPECIAL SCREEN: read the record, gate or not?
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC23. $EECC reads the map record at $E4 and returns its byte 2 in A. Bit 7 set = a CORRIDOR GATE (byte 2 AND $7F is the corridor), clear = another kind of special screen ($EE56). The screen type, 0-8, ends up in $51 (in the labyrinth $51 is the screen type) and the scene is $10 + the type. RUN: $EE1D called from the labyrinth savestate with the position set through bank 5 $802D (with $A4 = 4) on every kind of special record.

regions.name: Gate: the corridor's reward item
regions.description: $55 := $EF40[corridor] (the item the cleared gate holds) and $15 := the corridor number.

regions.name: Gate: has the corridor been cleared?
regions.description: JSR $EFAC tests bit (corridor - 1) of the cleared flags $04A9/$04AA: carry CLEAR = cleared, SET = not cleared. Not cleared goes to $EE3C.

regions.name: Gate, cleared: type 4 or 5
regions.description: $30 bit 6 set -> screen type 5, clear -> type 4. Bit 6 is still set from the corridor just played, so type 5 is the gate seen on RETURNING from the corridor (the ship's scripted entrance $F4B7 follows, and one door cell is opened); type 4 is the same gate on every later visit. RUN: $EE1D called from the labyrinth savestate with the position set through bank 5 $802D (with $A4 = 4) on every kind of special record. Corridor 5 cleared: bit 6 set gave type 5, bit 6 clear gave type 4.

regions.name: Gate, not cleared: sealed gate (8), or corridor 21's special rule
regions.description: Corridors 1-20: type 8, the SEALED GATE (two type-$35 halves, see the seal notes). Corridor 21 ($15 = $15): ($04AA OR $FC) AND $04A9 = $FF means corridors 1-10 are all cleared -> type 8, otherwise type 0 (the gate is shut, no seal puzzle). A cleared corridor 21 takes the cleared path above (type 4 / 5). RUN: nothing cleared 0; 1-9 cleared 0; 1-10 cleared 8; 1-10 and 21 cleared 4.

regions.name: Not a gate: the screen kind from byte 2's low nibble
regions.description: Nibble 1 (the progress recorder) and 3 (a message) keep their number. Nibble 2 and 6 are the round creature's shops: the sub-id $5E is tested in the item flags ($EFE0: the $04A0 array); flag clear keeps 2 / 6, flag SET (already bought) gives 7, the shop after buying. RUN: nibble 2 and 6 gave 2 / 6, and 7 with the flags set; 1 and 3 unchanged.

regions.name: Special screen: scene, area 0, flags
regions.description: $51 := the type, $5C := $10 + the type (the scene number), bank 5 $8000 loads the scene (tile list, metatile sets, palettes), $50 := 0, $30 := ($30 AND $8F) OR $20: the special-screen flag set, the corridor/boss bits cleared. RUN: $30 = $20 afterwards.

regions.name: Special screen: build the room buffer
regions.description: Bank 5 $8003 (-> $8155) builds the 16 x 12 buffer from the type's structure, door set and item list.

regions.name: Special screen type 5: open the gate
regions.description: Only for type 5: the four buffer cells $0740 + $37, + $72, + $7D, + $A7 that hold metatile 8 (the door) become metatile $0C (open), through $EEB7. RUN: in corridor 5's gate the cell at +$72 went 8 -> 12 for type 5 and stayed 8 for types 4 and 8 (the other three cells held other metatiles in this gate's layout).

regions.name: Special screen: classes, draw, and the screen's objects
regions.description: Bank 5 $8006 (the cell classes), $EFF3 with A = $20 (draw the whole room into nametable 0, spawning the ground objects), bank 5 $8036 (-> $A430: the screen's own set-up; not read).

regions.name: Special screen: slot 5 and the screen's sound
regions.description: $0505 (slot 5's type) := $35, the gate halves' type, for every special screen (the screens that have no gate presumably overwrite or ignore it; not checked); then A = $EF21[type] and, if not 0, JMP $D852 plays it. The table is indexed by the SCREEN TYPE 0-8: $10 $18 $18 $13 $10 0 $18 $18 $12. RUN: sounds $10 (type 0), $18 (1, 2, 6, 7), $13 (3), $10 (4), none (5), $12 (8). CORRECTION: tbl_EF21 was labelled 'corridor sound, first 9 corridors' (a lead) from the misreading that $51 is a corridor here.

regions.name: Open one door cell
regions.description: In: X = an offset into the room buffer $0740. If the cell holds metatile 8 it becomes $0C.

regions.name: Common start of every room load: read the record
regions.description: $56 := $FF (no pick-up box open), $EE09 loads the attribute patterns, bank 5 $8015 reads the map record at $E4 (set by $802D), bank 5 $8000 with A = 0 loads the common scene 0, and A := the record's byte 2 (Y = 2). Called by the special-screen loader, the ordinary-room loader and the corridor loader ($EF6C).

regions.name: LOAD AN ORDINARY ROOM: byte 2 gives the area
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC76 and the room paths. A = byte 2 of the record: its HIGH nibble -> $51 (what it means for an ordinary room was not worked out), its LOW nibble -> $50, the labyrinth AREA 0-10; the scene is $5C = area + 5 (so area n is scene n + 5, after the common scenes 0 and 32). RUN: area 0 -> scene 5.

regions.name: Ordinary room: scene, buffer, classes
regions.description: Bank 5 $8000 loads the scene; $30 AND $8F (the special-screen, corridor and boss bits off); $8003 builds the room buffer, $8030 (-> $A3BB: the layout's items and gates: not read through here) and $8006 the cell classes.

regions.name: Ordinary room: draw, and set up the screen's objects
regions.description: $EFF3 with A = $20 draws the room into nametable 0 and spawns its ground objects; bank 5 $8039 (-> $A462: the room's enemy set-up; not read through here).

regions.name: Ordinary room: the area's music
regions.description: A := $EF16[$50] (the labyrinth music by area: 09 07 07 02 02 07 0D 07 02 0D 0E) and JMP $D852 plays it. RUN: area 0 played sound 9.
